citations.excerpt:
Instead, we define a flexible program whose behavior is determined by a
number of  parameters

citations.label: Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai), chapter 1 Introduction (parameters as knobs)
citations.excerpt:
You can think of the parameters as knobs that we can turn, manipulating
the behavior of the program.

citations.label: Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai), chapter 1 Introduction (a fixed setting is a model)
citations.excerpt:
Once the parameters are fixed, we call the
program a  model

citations.label: Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai), chapter 1 Introduction (learning algorithm chooses parameters)
citations.excerpt:
the “meta-program” that uses our
dataset to choose the parameters is called a  learning algorithm

citations.label: Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai), chapter 1 Introduction (learning as finding the setting)
citations.excerpt:
In machine learning, the  learning  is the process by
which we discover the right setting of the knobs for coercing the
desired behavior from our model.

citations.label: Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai), chapter 1 Introduction (performance improves with experience)
citations.excerpt:
As a machine learning algorithm accumulates more experience,
typically in the form of observational data or interactions with an
environment, its performance improves.

citations.label: Wikipedia, Machine learning (supervised model of inputs and outputs)
citations.excerpt: Supervised learning algorithms build a mathematical model of a set of data that contains both the inputs and the desired outputs.

citations.label: Wikipedia, Machine learning (learning a predictive function)
citations.excerpt: supervised learning algorithms learn a function that can be used to predict the output associated with new inputs.

citations.label: Wikipedia, Machine learning (learning as loss minimisation)
citations.excerpt: Many learning problems are formulated as minimisation of some  loss function  on a training set of examples.

citations.label: Wikipedia, Machine learning (what a loss function expresses)
citations.excerpt: Loss functions express the discrepancy between the predictions of the model being trained and the actual problem instances

citations.label: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Linear regression module (what linear regression finds)
citations.excerpt:
In an ML
context, linear regression finds the relationship between
  features   and a
  label

citations.label: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Linear regression module (training adjusts weights and bias)
citations.excerpt: During training, the model adjusts its bias (b) and weights (w) to minimize the difference between predicted and actual values.

citations.label: Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai), section 3.1 Linear Regression (simplest standard tool)
citations.excerpt:
Linear regression  is both the simplest and most popular among the
standard tools for tackling regression problems.

citations.label: Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai), section 3.1 Linear Regression (what the weights do)
citations.excerpt:
The weights determine the influence of each feature on our
prediction.

citations.label: Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai), section 3.1 Linear Regression (squared error loss)
citations.excerpt:
For regression problems, the most common loss function is the squared
error.

citations.label: Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai), section 3.1 Linear Regression (iterative error reduction)
citations.excerpt:
The key technique for optimizing nearly every deep learning model, and
which we will call upon throughout this book, consists of iteratively
reducing the error by updating the parameters in the direction that
incrementally lowers the loss function.

citations.label: Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai), section 3.1 Linear Regression (hyperparameters are not learned)
citations.excerpt:
Frequently minibatch size and learning
rate are user-defined. Such tunable parameters that are not updated in
the training loop are called  hyperparameters
